# What scripts/measure measures, one workload per line: a name (letters,
# digits, _ . -), then -q if the program prints its result (its output
# is then thrown away), -p <program> if the command only starts the
# measured program (time runs only, no count), and -c <cycles> for a
# sampling period of its own (it wins over measure's -c), then the
# command, with paths from the repo folder. Words are split at spaces
# and quotes are not understood; extra spaces only line the columns up.
# record keeps each name to one command, so a changed command needs a
# new name.
#
# The compile workloads sample every 1,000,003 cycles, not every
# 100,003: a gcc build of git runs for minutes, and the default would
# write about 200 MB of samples per run.
